name: Lordship of Milan
alt: Della Torre and Visconti lordship of Milan

successors.name: Duchy of Milan
successors.text: the Visconti lands in 1395 without the Montferrat holdings

ledger.x: May 1259: Martino della Torre becomes lord of Milan.
December 1263: Como is annexed.
1270: Lodi falls to Milan.
1271: Como revolts.
1271: Lodi revolts, a year after it fell (same sentence as Como).
21 January 1277: Archbishop Ottone Visconti beats the Della Torre.
1302: the Della Torre force Matteo Visconti out.
After 1313: Matteo and Galeazzo become lords of other cities.
After 1313: Como and Novara.
20 September 1313: the Visconti are back for good.
1315: Pavia is captured.
1334: Cremona surrenders.
1337: Luchino enters Brescia.
1340: Luchino takes Asti.
1346: Parma. 'In 1346 Luchino took Parma.'
1347: Luchino pushes the western border.
ledger.cp: Piedmont lords (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1347: Alba and Chieri, as a bridge (confidence 1).
ledger.cp: Piedmont lords (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1350: Giovanni Visconti gets Bologna.
1353: Genoa accepts Giovanni Visconti's lordship.
October 1354: the Visconti domains are divided.
1356: Genoa throws off the Visconti lordship.
1356: Pavia passes out of Visconti hands.
1356: Montferrat takes Alba, Mondovi and Chieri.
1356: Novara leaves Visconti hands, as a bridge (confidence 1).
ledger.cp: league against Milan (taker not named by the page)

ledger.x: 23 January 1356: Montferrat occupies Asti.
June 1356: Cuneo goes to Philip II of Taranto.
8 June 1358: Alba returns to the Visconti.
8 June 1358: Novara returns to the Visconti (same sentence as Alba).
ledger.cp: league against Milan (taker not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1359: Pavia surrenders.
1370: Casale is conquered.
1379: Asti submits.
5-6 May 1385: Gian Galeazzo overthrows Bernabo.
19 October 1387: Antonio della Scala flees Verona before Gian Galeazzo.

1388: Padua. 'A military campaign between 1386 and 1388 ended with the conquest of the Della Scala and' (truncated); Gian Galeazzo page: 'took Verona, Vicenza, and Padua'. The year of Padua is not on the pages; 1388 is the campaign's end.
1389: Asti leaves the Visconti in a dowry.
ledger.cp: Louis of Valois, Duke of Orleans

ledger.x: 1390: Padua reverts to the Carrara.
5 September 1395: the lordship becomes a duchy.

wars.name: Scaliger War
wars.outcome: The league of Florence, Venice, Siena, Bologna, Perugia and, from 1337, Milan, the Este and the Gonzaga broke Mastino II della Scala, whose lands were reduced to Verona and Vicenza; Milan took Brescia in 1337.

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundaries; every extent is a province-level or town-circle reading of dated acquisitions.
